mainTopic: The end of עזרא's enactments, the ten special laws of ירושלים, and the siege story behind the ban on pigs and חכמת יוונית
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining the ten enactments of עזרא. It explains that he added combing the hair before immersion and had peddlers travel through the towns so women could get cosmetics. It also explains his enactment of טבילה for a בעל קרי: the Torah requires it only for תרומה and קדשים, and עזרא extended it to learning Torah. Next, a ברייתא lists ten special laws of ירושלים, and the גמרא explains each one. Four come from פסוקים, because this תנא holds that ירושלים was never given to any one שבט. Five have practical reasons, such as protecting טהרה, keeping the pilgrims safe, and avoiding smoke and smell, and one is simply a tradition. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's ban on raising pigs and tells the story of the war in בית חשמונאי, where a pig sent up the wall made ארץ ישראל shake. Because of that story, the חכמים cursed raising pigs and teaching חכמת יוונית. The גמרא begins to question that second curse with a ברייתא from רבי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: עזרא added combing the hair
steps.stepSummary: Finishing an earlier answer: the Torah only requires checking the hair, and עזרא added the requirement to actually comb it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he (עזרא) came and enacted combing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing an answer it started just before this. It says that the requirement to comb the hair is an addition by עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question before this was that combing the hair seems to be a Torah law already. The answer is that the Torah only requires checking the hair to make sure nothing blocks the water. עזרא went further and required real combing even when nothing is knotted.

keyTerms.meaning: Combing or washing the hair, done before immersion
He enacted, he set up a rule
He came (used to mean he took action and added something)

phrases.english: And he came
phrases.notes: "He" is עזרא. This finishes the answer from just before: the Torah only requires checking the hair.

phrases.english: and enacted combing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from the previous section of the daf about combing hair.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the law into levels: the Torah requires the basic level, and עזרא added more
steps.terutzMaskana: Combing the hair is a rabbinic addition by עזרא on top of the Torah's requirement to check the hair.

steps.title: Why peddlers should travel through the towns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that עזרא had peddlers travel through the towns so that women could buy cosmetics and jewelry and stay attractive to their husbands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that peddlers should travel around the towns: this is because of women's jewelry and cosmetics, so that the women will not become unattractive to their husbands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next enactment of עזרא, about traveling peddlers, and gives the reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody asks a question here. The גמרא simply gives the reason. Peddlers carried women's cosmetics and jewelry, so having them visit every town made sure women everywhere could get these things and keep a happy marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: Go around, travel from place to place

phrases.english: And that peddlers should travel around the towns:
this is because of women's cosmetics,
so that they will not become unattractive to their husbands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the list of עזרא's enactments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Peddlers must travel through the towns so that women can get cosmetics and stay attractive to their husbands.

steps.title: Isn't immersion after an emission already a Torah law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes עזרא's enactment of טבילה for a בעל קרי and asks how this can be his enactment when a פסוק in the Torah already requires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he enacted immersion for those who had a seminal emission. But that is a Torah law! As it is written: "And if a man has an emission of seed, he shall wash his flesh in water."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last of עזרא's ten enactments and immediately challenges it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An enactment is supposed to be something new. If the Torah already tells a בעל קרי to wash in water, it seems that עזרא added nothing. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Men who had a seminal emission
From the Torah, a Torah law

phrases.english: And he enacted immersion for those who had a seminal emission.
But it is a Torah law! As it is written:
"And if a man has an emission of seed,
he shall wash his flesh in water"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next enactment, then challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that טבילה for a בעל קרי is an enactment of עזרא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק already requires it, so it cannot be something new that עזרא started.

steps.title: עזרא extended טבילה to Torah learning
steps.stepSummary: The Torah requires טבילה only for eating תרומה and קדשים. עזרא extended it so that a בעל קרי must immerse even before learning Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: By Torah law it is required for תרומה and קדשים. He (עזרא) came and enacted it even for words of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The Torah's requirement is limited, and עזרא's enactment adds a new situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, a בעל קרי only has to immerse before eating holy food like תרומה or קדשים. עזרא's new rule was that he must also immerse before saying or learning Torah. So the enactment is real, because it covers something the Torah did not.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן, eaten only in purity
Words of Torah, learning or saying Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying the פסוק doesn't count. The Torah law stays fully in place for תרומה and קדשים. עזרא only added Torah learning on top of it.
steps.whatToRemember: Several of עזרא's enactments follow one pattern: the Torah sets a basic requirement, and עזרא extends it. This is true of combing the hair and of טבילה for a בעל קרי.

phrases.english: By Torah law it is required for teruma and sacrificial food;
he came and enacted it
even for words of Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the Torah law: the Torah covers some situations, and the enactment adds a new one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the Torah requires immersion, עזרא added nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah requires immersion only for תרומה and קדשים. עזרא required it even for learning Torah.

steps.title: Ten special laws of ירושלים: the first three
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists ten laws unique to ירושלים. The first three are: a house sold there never becomes permanently sold, it never brings an עגלה ערופה, and it can never become an עיר הנדחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ten things were said about ירושלים: a house in it does not become permanently sold; it does not bring an עגלה ערופה; and it cannot become an עיר הנדחת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, a ברייתא about ירושלים. It connects to the משנה's rule that chickens may not be raised there. This step brings the opening line of the list and its first three items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item takes a regular Torah law and says it does not apply in ירושלים. Normally a house sold in a walled city becomes the buyer's forever if it is not bought back within a year, but not in ירושלים. ירושלים is also excluded from bringing an עגלה ערופה and from becoming an עיר הנדחת.

keyTerms.meaning: Permanently sold, can no longer be bought back
The calf whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown
A city whose people turned to idol worship and which is destroyed

steps.whyThisMatters: These laws show that ירושלים has a special status. In some ways it is treated differently from every other city in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Ten things were said about Jerusalem:
a house in it does not become permanently sold;
phrases.notes: In other walled cities, a sold house becomes the buyer's forever if it isn't bought back within a year. That doesn't happen in ירושלים.

phrases.english: and it does not bring a heifer whose neck is broken;
and it cannot become an idolatrous city;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of עזרא's enactments and returns to the משנה's law about ירושלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house in ירושלים never becomes permanently sold, ירושלים does not bring an עגלה ערופה, and it cannot become an עיר הנדחת.

steps.title: The rest of the list of special laws for ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the remaining seven special laws of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A house in ירושלים does not become impure with נגעים. People may not build projections or balconies sticking out over the street. No garbage dumps, no kilns, and no gardens or orchards, except the rose gardens that were there since the days of the early prophets. No raising chickens, and no leaving a dead body there overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step keeps going and finishes its list of ten laws that apply only to ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5 and 6 together give the full list of ten. Most of these new laws protect the cleanliness, beauty and טהרה of the holy city. The one exception is the old rose gardens, which were already there from the time of the early prophets.

keyTerms.meaning: Leprous-type marks that can make a house impure
Beams or ledges that stick out from a building

phrases.english: And it does not become impure with leprous marks;
phrases.notes: "It" here means a house in ירושלים.

phrases.english: and one may not build projections or balconies out over its streets;
and one may not make garbage dumps in it;
and one may not build kilns in it;
and one may not plant gardens and orchards in it –
except for the rose gardens
that were there from the days of the early prophets;
and one may not raise chickens in it;
and one may not leave a dead body in it overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of ten laws begun in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירושלים has seven more special restrictions: no נגעים on houses, no projections, garbage dumps, kilns, gardens (except the old rose gardens), chickens, or overnight corpses.

steps.title: Why a house in ירושלים is never permanently sold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק showing that a permanent sale needs a buyer who truly owns the house, and ירושלים never belonged to a שבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: A house in ירושלים does not become permanently sold, because the פסוק says: "the house in the walled city shall belong permanently to the one who bought it, for his generations." And this תנא holds that ירושלים was never divided among the שבטים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back through the list one law at a time. It starts with the first law and gives its source in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a house in a walled city that is not bought back within a year stays with the buyer forever. But this תנא holds ירושלים belongs to all of כלל ישראל, not to any one שבט. So nobody really owns a house there in the normal way, and the rule of a permanent sale does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Permanently sold, with no chance to buy it back
A house in a city surrounded by a wall
Was not divided up among the tribes

phrases.english: A house in it does not become permanently sold –
as it is written: "Then the house that is in the walled city shall stand
permanently to the one who bought it, for his generations,"
and he holds that ירושלים was not divided among the tribes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the list, starting with the first law from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The law that a house in ירושלים never becomes permanently sold.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 25:30 together with the view that ירושלים was not divided among the שבטים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea, ירושלים was not given to any שבט, that the גמרא will use again for the next two laws.

steps.title: Why ירושלים does not bring an עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק of עגלה ערופה speaks of land given 'to possess it,' and ירושלים was never given to a שבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: ירושלים does not bring an עגלה ערופה, because the פסוק says: "If a dead body is found in the land that ה׳ your God gives you to possess." And ירושלים was not divided among the שבטים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second law on the list and gives its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the land as given to you "to possess." Since ירושלים was never handed to any single שבט as their share, it does not fit this description. So the עגלה ערופה ritual does not apply there.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown
To possess it, to inherit it

phrases.english: And it does not bring a calf whose neck is broken –
as it is written: "If a slain person is found in the land

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ נוֹתֵן לְךָ לְרִשְׁתָּהּ״,
phrases.english: that ה׳ your God gives you to possess it,"
and ירושלים was not divided among the tribes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same idea from step 7 to explain the second law.
steps.raayaObject: The law that ירושלים does not bring an עגלה ערופה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 21:1 ('to possess it') together with the view that ירושלים was not divided among the שבטים.

steps.title: Why ירושלים can never become an עיר הנדחת
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק of עיר הנדחת says 'your cities,' and ירושלים never belonged to a single שבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: ירושלים cannot become an עיר הנדחת, because the פסוק says "your cities." And ירושלים was not divided among the שבטים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third law on the list, again using the same reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of "your cities," meaning cities that belong to a particular group. Since ירושלים belongs to everyone and not to one שבט, it is not counted as one of "your cities." So it can never be judged as an עיר הנדחת.

keyTerms.meaning: A city whose people were led to worship idols and is destroyed

steps.whatToRemember: The first three special laws of ירושלים (no permanent house sale, no עגלה ערופה, no עיר הנדחת) all come from one idea: this תנא holds that ירושלים was never given to any single שבט. The next step (Step 10) uses the same idea for a fourth law, נגעים.

phrases.english: And it cannot become an idolatrous city –
as it is written: "your cities,"
and ירושלים was not divided among the tribes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same idea from steps 7 and 8 to explain the third law.
steps.raayaObject: The law that ירושלים can never become an עיר הנדחת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 13:13 ('your cities') together with the view that ירושלים was not divided among the שבטים.

steps.title: A house in ירושלים cannot become impure with נגעים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק of נגעי בתים, which speaks of 'the land of your possession.' Since ירושלים was never divided among the שבטים, its houses are not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: A house in ירושלים does not become impure through נגעים, because the פסוק says 'a house of the land of your possession,' and ירושלים was not divided among the שבטים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the next law on the list: houses in ירושלים cannot become impure with צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works the same way as the last few steps. The פסוק limits נגעי בתים to 'the land of your possession,' meaning land that belongs to a שבט. ירושלים was never given to any single שבט, so the law of נגעים does not apply there.

keyTerms.meaning: Marks of צרעת (a spiritual 'leprosy') that can appear on people, clothing or houses

phrases.english: And it does not become impure with leprous marks
as it is written: "And I will put a plague of leprosy
in a house of the land of your possession",
and Jerusalem was not divided among the tribes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same reasoning as steps 7-9 for another law from the ברייתא's list.
steps.raayaObject: The law that houses in ירושלים cannot become impure with נגעים
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 14:34, 'בבית ארץ אחזתכם,' together with the fact that ירושלים was not divided among the שבטים

steps.title: No projections or balconies in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: Houses in ירושלים may not have projections or balconies sticking out over the street. There are two reasons: they could spread טומאה through אהל, and they could injure the crowds of pilgrims.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not build projections or balconies sticking out from houses in ירושלים. One reason is that they act as a 'tent' that can spread the impurity of a dead body. The other is so the pilgrims are not hurt by bumping into them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next law on the list. This time it gives practical reasons, not a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A roof over even a small piece of a dead body makes everyone under that roof impure. ירושלים is full of people who need to stay טהור for קרבנות, so a balcony over the street is a danger. The second reason is simple safety, because the streets are packed with עולי רגלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Projections or ledges sticking out from a wall
A 'tent' of impurity: a covering that spreads the impurity of a dead body to everything under it
Pilgrims who come up to ירושלים for the festivals

phrases.english: And one may not build out in it
projections and balconies –
because of a tent of impurity,
phrases.notes: If a piece of a dead body is under the balcony, everyone who walks under it becomes impure.

phrases.english: and so that the pilgrims are not injured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from laws that come from a פסוק to a law explained by practical reasons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Projections and balconies are not allowed in ירושלים, because of אהל הטומאה and the safety of the pilgrims.

steps.title: No garbage heaps in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: Garbage heaps may not be made in ירושלים, because they attract שקצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not make garbage heaps in ירושלים, because of creeping creatures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason for the next law on the list: no garbage dumps in the city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Garbage heaps attract creeping creatures. When these creatures die they make things impure, which would threaten the טהרה that people need in ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Creeping creatures and vermin that can carry impurity

phrases.english: And one may not make garbage heaps in it –
because of creeping creatures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practical reason, once again about protecting the טהרה of ירושלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Garbage heaps are not allowed in ירושלים because of שקצים.

steps.title: No kilns in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: Kilns may not be built in ירושלים, because of their smoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not build kilns in ירושלים, because of the smoke.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason for the next law: no kilns (big ovens) in ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason is different from the last two. It is not about טומאה. It is about keeping ירושלים clean and beautiful, since smoke from kilns would blacken the city.

keyTerms.meaning: Kilns, large ovens for pottery or lime

steps.whatToRemember: The special laws of ירושלים come from two kinds of sources. Some come from פסוקים, because ירושלים never belonged to one שבט (a permanent sale, עגלה ערופה, עיר הנדחת, נגעים). Others come from practical reasons: protecting טהרה, keeping the pilgrims safe, and keeping the city beautiful.

phrases.english: And one may not make kilns in it –
because of the smoke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with a new kind of reason: the city's appearance instead of טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kilns are not allowed in ירושלים because of their smoke.

steps.title: No gardens or orchards in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: Gardens and orchards may not be planted in ירושלים because of the bad smell they give off.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not make gardens or orchards in ירושלים, because of the bad smell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues down the list of special rules for ירושלים. This rule bans gardens and orchards and gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the kilns in Step 13, this rule protects the city from something unpleasant rather than from טומאה. Here the problem is the smell that gardens and orchards give off.

phrases.english: And one may not make in it
gardens and orchards
because of the bad smell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list of ירושלים rules, with its reason
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No gardens or orchards in ירושלים, because of the smell.

steps.title: No raising chickens in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: Chickens may not be raised in ירושלים because of the קדשים eaten there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not raise chickens in ירושלים, because of the holy foods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next rule on the list. Chickens are banned in ירושלים, and the reason has to do with the holy food eaten in the city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the smoke and smell rules just before it, this reason is not about comfort. It is about protecting the קדשים from becoming טמא, much like the reasons for banning balconies and garbage heaps.

phrases.english: And one may not raise chickens in it
because of the holy foods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No chickens in ירושלים, to protect the קדשים.

steps.title: No leaving a dead body overnight: a tradition
steps.stepSummary: A dead body may not be left overnight in ירושלים. This rule is a received tradition with no reason given.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not leave a dead body overnight in ירושלים. This is a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last rule on the list. It says this one is simply a tradition that was passed down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other rule had a reason. The first four came from פסוקים (Steps 7-10), and the rest had practical reasons (Steps 11-15). Here the גמרא gives no reason at all and just says the rule comes from tradition.
steps.confusionAlert: The word גמרא here does not mean 'the Talmud.' It means a tradition that was learned and passed down.
steps.whatToRemember: The list of special rules for ירושלים is now complete. Four come from פסוקים, because ירושלים was never given to one שבט. Five have practical reasons (טומאה, crowds, smoke, smell). The rule about a dead body is a pure tradition.

phrases.english: And one may not leave a dead body overnight in it
it is a tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item in the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dead body is not left overnight in ירושלים, based on tradition.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: no raising pigs anywhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that pigs may not be raised anywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not raise pigs in any place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next rule. This sets up the story that will explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic. Unlike the ירושלים rules, the ban on pigs applies everywhere, not just in one city.

phrases.english: One may not raise pigs
in any place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pigs may not be raised anywhere.

steps.title: The civil war in בית חשמונאי and the תמידים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא begins the story. When the two brothers of בית חשמונאי fought, הורקנוס was inside ירושלים and אריסטובלוס was outside. Each day the people inside lowered money in a box, and the people outside sent up animals for the תמידים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: When the family of בית חשמונאי fought each other, הורקנוס was inside the city and אריסטובלוס was outside. Every day the people inside lowered coins to the others in a box, and the others sent up animals for the תמידים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the background story for the pig rule. This step only sets the scene, and the story continues in Step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even during a siege, the people found a way to keep bringing the תמיד every day. The money went down and the animals came up. Something in this arrangement will soon go wrong, and that will lead to the ban on pigs.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁצָּרוּ בֵּית חַשְׁמוֹנַאי זֶה עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: When members of the Hasmonean house besieged one another,
Hyrcanus was inside
and Aristobulus was outside.
And every day they would lower down to them
coins in a box,
and they would send up to them animals for the daily offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּשֶׁצָּרוּ בֵּית חַשְׁמוֹנַאי זֶה עַל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the background story for the משנה's pig rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Background: during the siege, money was lowered and animals for the תמיד were sent up each day.

steps.title: The elder's advice and the pig on the wall
steps.stepSummary: An elder who knew חכמת יוונית told the besiegers that ירושלים would stay safe as long as the עבודה went on. The next day they sent up a pig instead of a קרבן animal, and when it reached halfway up the wall, ארץ ישראל shook.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an old man there who knew חכמת יוונית. He told the besiegers: as long as the people inside keep doing the עבודה, you will not beat them. The next day the people inside lowered money in a box as usual, but the besiegers sent up a pig. When the pig got halfway up the wall, it dug its hooves in, and all of ארץ ישראל shook, 400 by 400 parasangs.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the siege story from Step 18. It tells how the daily animal for the תמיד was replaced with a pig, and how the land shook in response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the deal had kept the עבודה going even during the war. The elder, using his חכמת יוונית, understood that the עבודה was protecting the city, so his advice was meant to stop it. The earthquake shows how terrible it was to send a pig toward the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The service of the קרבנות in the בית המקדש
A parasang, a large measure of distance

phrases.english: There was a certain elder there
who was familiar with Greek wisdom.
He said to them:
phrases.notes: "Them" means the besiegers outside the city, the side of אריסטובלוס.

phrases.english: As long as they are busy with the Temple service,
they will not be handed over to you.
The next day they lowered coins in a box,
and they sent up to them a pig.
When it reached halfway up the wall,
it stuck its hooves into the wall,
and the land of Israel shook

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת פַּרְסָה עַל אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת פַּרְסָה.
phrases.english: four hundred parasangs by four hundred parasangs.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה שָׁם זָקֵן אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה מַכִּיר בְּחׇכְמַת יְווֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the siege story from Step 18 and describes the turning point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sending a pig in place of the תמיד animal caused ארץ ישראל to shake. This story is the background for the curses that follow.

steps.title: The two curses: raising pigs and teaching חכמת יוונית
steps.stepSummary: Because of what happened, the חכמים cursed anyone who raises pigs and anyone who teaches his son חכמת יוונית.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that time the חכמים said: Cursed is the man who raises pigs, and cursed is the man who teaches his son חכמת יוונית.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reaches its main point: two curses that came out of the story. This explains the source of the משנה's rule against raising pigs that was quoted in Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each curse matches one part of the story. The pig was the tool used against the עבודה, and חכמת יוונית was what gave the elder his idea. So both the tool and the wisdom behind it were cursed.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on raising pigs and the curse on teaching חכמת יוונית both come from this one story of the siege.
steps.whyThisMatters: This curse on חכמת יוונית is what the גמרא is about to question in Step 22.

phrases.english: At that time they said:
Cursed is the man who raises pigs,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָרוּר הָאָדָם שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד אֶת בְּנוֹ חׇכְמַת יְווֹנִית.
phrases.english: and cursed is the person who teaches his son Greek wisdom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the halachic result out of the story told in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is cursed to raise pigs, and it is cursed to teach one's son חכמת יוונית.

steps.title: A משנה about the עומר and שתי הלחם is linked to the siege
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that a משנה describing the עומר brought from גנות הצריפין and the שתי הלחם brought from בקעת עין סוכר refers to that same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about that time we learned in a משנה: It once happened that the barley for the עומר came from גנות הצריפין, and the wheat for the שתי הלחם came from בקעת עין סוכר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by connecting a known משנה to this siege. It tells us which time period that unusual event happened in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the עומר and שתי הלחם being brought from unusual faraway places. The ברייתא explains that this happened during the war between the brothers. This closes the story.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות

phrases.english: And about that time we learned:
It once happened that the omer came from the gardens of Tzerifin,
and the two loaves came from the valley of Ein Sokher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא by tying a known משנה to the same siege.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה about the עומר from גנות הצריפין and the שתי הלחם from בקעת עין סוכר took place during this siege.

steps.title: Is חכמת יוונית really forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the curse on חכמת יוונית by starting to quote a ברייתא in which רבי speaks about ארץ ישראל. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is חכמת יוונית really forbidden? But we learned in a ברייתא: רבי said: In ארץ ישראל –
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the curse from Step 20 and starts bringing a ברייתא from רבי to challenge it. The quote is cut off here, so this step is setting up the challenge that continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said that teaching חכמת יוונית is cursed. The words "מי אסירא" signal that the גמרא knows a source suggesting it is allowed or even valued. We will see what רבי actually said when the text continues.
steps.confusionAlert: The quote from רבי is not finished here. Do not try to guess his point yet; it continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: But is Greek wisdom really forbidden?!
But we learned in a baraita: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name always means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: In the land of Israel –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second curse in Step 20, the curse on teaching חכמת יוונית.
steps.kashyaTarget: The curse on anyone who teaches his son חכמת יוונית (Step 20).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא from רבי seems to show that חכמת יוונית is not forbidden, which clashes with the curse. The full quote continues past this section.
